binders: A dimension m, vector field q, flux, proposed derivative map fluxDerivative, point x,t, and vector qx.
hypotheses: The spatial slice xi -> q(xi,t) has derivative qx at x.
flux has Fréchet derivative fluxDerivative(q(x,t)) at q(x,t).
conclusions: The conservative residual q_t+(flux(q))_x=0 at (x,t) holds if and only if the quasilinear residual q_t+fluxDerivative(q(x,t))(q_x)=0 holds there.
mathematical_definitions: The conservative predicate existentially witnesses q_t and the derivative of xi -> flux(q(xi,t)).
The quasilinear predicate existentially witnesses q_t and q_x and applies the supplied continuous linear derivative of flux.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Under pointwise differentiability of q in space and Fréchet differentiability of the flux at the current state, the conservative differential form is equivalent to the quasilinear chain-rule form using the flux derivative.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension m is unrestricted and may be zero.
The assumptions are pointwise; no global smoothness is asserted.
No time differentiability is assumed separately, so if a time derivative does not exist both residual predicates can be false.
The fluxDerivative function is only constrained at the single state q(x,t), not globally.
